prompt:
Create ONE revised full-body character illustration based on image 1, guided by the refined 2D painting and purposeful bright light accents of image 2. The user specifically rejects the plastic-toy hair and fragmented lighting of image 1. They explicitly WANT some beautiful intense highlights and localized luminous light effects like the reference. Do not make another uniformly subdued version.

Preserve the recognizable adult red-haired female archer, mature amber-eyed face, strong low grounded drawing-the-bow pose, and the newer silver-gray light armor / rich purple cloth / dark leather design direction. The costume is flexible: simplify small seams and competing ornament as useful for a more unified design. Do not return to all-over gold armor or white skirt lining. Retain coherent anatomy and correct bow, arrow, string and hand mechanics. Allow a little more transparent margin so the whole bow, arrowhead and feet fit.

1. COMPLETELY REDRAW THE HAIR SHAPES AND HAIR SHADING.
Image 1's ponytail is made of thick molded curls: the big loops at image left and hooked ends have repeated thickness, rounded rims, separate dark grooves and separate bright strips. Replace that geometry. Make the long crimson high ponytail one coherent, gravity-aware flowing volume sweeping toward image left, with a thick gathered root, overlapping thin sheets of hair, and increasingly fine taper toward the ends. Neighboring locks merge into the common body of hair; only a few tips separate. Vary the width, length, overlap and edge sharpness. Merge the repeated open loops and rolled hooks into a natural main sweep. Retain elegant movement and abundant hair, without a tangle of individual flyaway strands.
Paint red hair with broad connected red midtones and shared deeper-red shadow shapes. Several neighboring locks share a light area. Fine drawn strand accents are sparse and directional. The forehead fringe has thin, slightly irregular tapering locks, never chunky extruded pieces. Avoid plastic tubes, rubber tentacles, ribbon rolls, sculpted toy grooves, thick bevels and polygonal highlight chips.

2. BUILD A DELIBERATE HIGH-LUMINANCE FOCAL REGION WITH A LOCAL LIGHT EFFECT.
Look closely at image 2: the crown/front hair has exceptionally bright light shapes, while pale luminous marks outside the crown and face-side silhouette support that focus. Borrow the arrangement, NOT the white hair color or the reference's whole poster layout.
Our archer keeps rich red hair. Concentrate warm vermilion/coral light in the crown and forehead-facing locks; place a small number of confidently shaped pale warm highlights at their most strongly lit turns. Keep most hair saturated crimson. Let the strongest highlights have a tiny soft luminous spill. Behind the upper crown and a short section of the outer hair beside the face, add a broken, asymmetrical pale cream-gold luminous wash with a bright local core and a short translucent falloff into alpha. It is a purposeful small light accent integrated with the head silhouette, not a circular halo, background rectangle, large glowing cloud, full-body rim, floating particles or scattered sparkles. No bright outlines around every strand. Do not bleach the entire hair mass or turn it silver/blond.
Use the same lighting logic to give the upper shoulder and one selected upper-chest armor turn a clear, elegant bright reflection. Let cheek and arm planes receive coherent softer light. The focus is the head, shoulder and drawn-arrow action. Keep quieter warm skin on the lower body and connected deep violet cloth shapes; no uniform top-to-bottom dark overlay.

3. UNIFY ARMOR AND CLOTH AROUND THAT FOCUS.
The armor has broad cool gray-blue / lavender-steel planes with restrained warm reflection near the head. Give a few focal edges genuinely bright accents. Across abdomen, waist, knees and boots remove disconnected white flecks and mosaic reflection islands. Model the main curved planes and actual overlap instead. Large middle-value areas remain intact. Purple cloth has rich stable local color and a few broad structural folds; consolidate many small angular value changes. Subdue decorative marks and nonessential seams outside the upper-body focal region. Rich detail is selective and integrated into the form.
Retain the reference's sophisticated 2D color-plane design, selective colored linework, real rounded volume and mixed crisp/soft/understated edges. Do not switch to glossy photorealistic 3D or smooth airbrushed plastic. Do not fake hand-painted quality with a full-surface paper texture, scratches, grain or mottled polygons.

DELIVER ONE complete finished illustration on actual alpha transparency, including the gaps within the pose and bow. The few localized luminous accents should fade cleanly to transparent pixels, with the rest of the background completely empty. No ground, scenery, typography, name, chibi, pedestal or checkerboard baked into the image. The localized head light effect is explicitly allowed and requested; do not remove all glow or all strong highlights.
